claims.source: Sol Foundation Science and Policy Briefings No. 3, Executive Summary
claims.text: The briefing states that the SIMS and MIBI analyses found no anomalous isotopic values but that the metals in the once-molten mass were mixed incompletely, 'indicating an industrial process of unknown, and potentially perplexing, origin'.

claims.source: Notes 11 and 12, Sol Foundation Briefing No. 3
claims.text: The briefing states that iron meteorites contain 5-40% nickel while the Council Bluffs sample had only trace amounts, and that aluminium oxide - the necessary byproduct of a thermite reaction - would have been observed as a diatomic in the SIMS analysis and was not.

The briefing records that no foundries in the region were operating on the day of the incident and that no airports or military facilities in the region reported aviation incidents before, during or after.

desc: A seven-page policy briefing published by The Sol Foundation in April 2026 and written by Marik von Rennenkampff, a former Obama-administration Department of Defense appointee and later State Department official. It is the most useful secondary document in this domain because it does what no journalism has: it sets out, with citations to contemporaneous 1977-1978 newspaper records and to the peer-reviewed paper, the full evidentiary structure of the Council Bluffs analysis - the witness accounts, the fire chief's description, the police photographs, the original 1978 identification of the material as high-carbon steel and slag, the 2021 SIMS and MIBI work at Stanford, and the systematic elimination of the meteorite, satellite, aircraft, dumping and thermite hypotheses with the specific physical reason for each rejection. Its conclusion is careful and correct: the analyses set 'an important standard for how rigorous scientific methods and cutting-edge materials analysis technologies can and should be applied to the study of UAP in the future.' It is also, read institutionally, a foundation telling Congress what a properly documented materials analysis looks like - which is a way of pointing at what the government's own holdings have never been subjected to in public.
